why: A class folder that no class of the project defines (as a built-in type's, `@double/f.m`) holds methods reached by their qualified name, the path rules picking the copy (project rule, qualifiedMethod in matlab-lookup.ts): `Crate.fluff(1)` calls `lib/@Crate/fluff.m`. Once a classdef `Crate.m` is added, `Crate` is that class, whose methods are those of its own file (MATLAB doc 'Class Precedence and MATLAB Path', 'Methods in Separate Files'): it has no `fluff`, and the call links nowhere; with the classdef deleted, the folder's method answers again. Each step must end where a fresh index ends (project rule).

edit.Crate.m:
classdef Crate
  methods
    function obj = Crate()
    end
  end
end
